from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

            # Fallback to center-right if grid key is invalid
            mobject.move_to(RIGHT * 3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            'Leonhard Euler discovered a profound connection to prime numbers.', 
            'The infinite sum equals an infinite product of primes.', 
            'Each prime p contributes a unique factor to Zeta.', 
            'This formula bridges integers and the building blocks of math.', 
            'Zeta encodes the secret distribution of all prime numbers.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Euler Product: The Bridge to Primes", lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # FOCUSED FIX: Using MarkupText instead of MathTex to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex' 
        # in environments where LaTeX is not installed. MarkupText uses Pango (system-level).
        sum_tex = MarkupText("Σ n<sup>-s</sup>", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(sum_tex, 'B1', 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        prod_tex = MarkupText("Π (1-p<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>", color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(prod_tex, 'B5', 'C6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(sum_tex))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(prod_tex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        expansion_parts = [
            "(1-2<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>",
            "(1-3<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>",
            "(1-5<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>",
            "(1-7<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>",
            "..."
        ]
        expansion = VGroup(*[MarkupText(part, color=GREEN, font_size=24) for part in expansion_parts]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(expansion, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(expansion, shift=UP))
        
        for i in range(4):
            self.play(Indicate(expansion[i], color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.3), run_time=0.7)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        bridge_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            sum_tex.get_right() + RIGHT*0.2, 
            prod_tex.get_left() + LEFT*0.2, 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_width=5
        )
        glow = bridge_arrow.copy().set_stroke(width=10, opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(bridge_arrow), FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Indicate(bridge_arrow, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        final_zeta = MarkupText(
            "ζ(s) = Σ n<sup>-s</sup> = Π (1-p<sup>-s</sup>)<sup>-1</sup>",
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(final_zeta, 'C1', 'E6', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(expansion),
            FadeOut(bridge_arrow),
            FadeOut(glow),
            Transform(sum_tex, final_zeta),
            Transform(prod_tex, final_zeta)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Initialization of the lesson
        title_str = "The Riemann Zeta Function: DNA of Primes"
        lines = [
            "- The Zeta Function Equation",
            "- The Euler Product Formula",
            "- Convergence and Analytic Continuity",
            "- Encoding Prime Distributions"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        )

        box = SurroundingRectangle(euler_product, color=RED, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(box))
        
        # Final emphasis
        conclusion = Text("Primes are the 'atoms' of Zeta", font_size=20, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section Context
        title = "The Million Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis"
        lines = [
            "Most zeros sit on a single vertical line.",
            "This critical line is where the real part is half.",
            "Riemann hypothesized that every non-trivial zero lies here.",
            "Proving this remains the greatest unsolved mystery in mathematics.",
            "A million-dollar prize awaits whoever solves this puzzle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Pre-build mobjects
        # 1. Boundaries and Strip
        line_left = Line(self.grid['B2'], self.grid['F2'], color="#808080", stroke_width=2)
        line_right = Line(self.grid['B4'], self.grid['F4'], color="#808080", stroke_width=2)
        
        label_0 = Text("x=0", font_size=16, color="#808080")
        self.place_at_grid(label_0, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0).shift(UP * 0.3)
        
        label_1 = Text("x=1", font_size=16, color="#808080")
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0).shift(UP * 0.3)
        
        strip = Rectangle(width=2, height=4, color="#E6E6FA", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(strip, 'B2', 'F4')
        
        # 2. Critical Line
        critical_line = Line(self.grid['B3'], self.grid['F3'], color="#FFD700", stroke_width=5)
        label_half = Text("x=1/2", font_size=18, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(label_half, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0).shift(UP * 0.4)
        
        # 3. Zeros (white dots)
        dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(self.grid[pos], color=WHITE, radius=0.08) 
            for pos in ['B3', 'C3', 'D3', 'E3', 'F3']
        ])
        # Slight aesthetic adjustments for zeros' spacing
        dots[0].shift(UP * 0.2)
        dots[1].shift(DOWN * 0.3)
        dots[2].shift(UP * 0.1)
        dots[3].shift(DOWN * 0.4)
        dots[4].shift(UP * 0.3)
        
        # 4. Prize text
        prize_text = Text("$1,000,000 Prize", font_size=32, color=WHITE, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_in_area(prize_text, 'A2', 'A5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match: #E6E6FA (Purple strip)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#E6E6FA"))
        self.play(
            Create(line_left), 
            Create(line_right), 
            FadeIn(strip), 
            Write(label_0), 
            Write(label_1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match: #FFD700 (Gold line)
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700")
        )
        self.play(Create(critical_line), Write(label_half))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match: #FFFFFF (White zeros)
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(dot, scale=0.5) for dot in dots], lag_ratio=0.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Color match: White
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(critical_line, color="#FFD700"), run_time=1.5)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Application: Cryptography and Prime Security"
        lines = [
            "Zeta's zeros act like the music of prime distribution.",
            "Understanding this music helps us predict prime locations.",
            "This security underpins modern digital encryption and privacy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Primes sequence at the bottom
        primes_vals = ["2", "3", "5", "7", "11"]
        prime_mobs = VGroup()
        grid_spots = ["F1", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"]
        
        for val, spot in zip(primes_vals, grid_spots):
            p_mob = Text(val, font_size=36, color="#00FFFF")
            self.place_at_grid(p_mob, spot)
            prime_mobs.add(p_mob)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(prime_mobs))
        
        # Pulsing animation for primes
        self.play(
            *[Indicate(p, color="#00FFFF", scale_factor=1.4) for p in prime_mobs],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Zeta Zeros represented as dots
        zeta_zeros = VGroup()
        zero_spots = ["B1", "B3", "B5", "C2", "C4", "C6"]
        for spot in zero_spots:
            dot = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
            self.place_at_grid(dot, spot)
            zeta_zeros.add(dot)
            
        self.play(Create(zeta_zeros))
        
        # Visualizing "music" - small waves or pulses from zeros
        waves = VGroup()
        for zero in zeta_zeros:
            wave = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#FF00FF", stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(zero.get_center())
            waves.add(wave)
            
        self.play(
            *[w.animate.scale(4).set_stroke(opacity=0) for w in waves],
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.remove(waves)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Silver padlock icon (#C0C0C0)
        padlock_body = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=1.0, fill_opacity=1, color="#C0C0C0")
        padlock_shackle = Arc(radius=0.4, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color="#C0C0C0", stroke_width=8)
        padlock_shackle.shift(UP * 0.5)
        padlock = VGroup(padlock_body, padlock_shackle)
        self.place_in_area(padlock, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(padlock))
        
        # Connections from Zeta Zeros to the Padlock
        connections = VGroup()
        for zero in zeta_zeros:
            line = Line(zero.get_center(), padlock.get_center(), color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.6)
            connections.add(line)
            
        self.play(Create(connections), run_time=2)
        
        # Final Highlight: pulse the lock and connections
        self.play(
            Indicate(padlock, color="#C0C0C0"),
            connections.animate.set_stroke(width=2, opacity=1),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: The DNA of Prime Numbers
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in calculus and complex numbers

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Harmonic Series and Convergence
sections.content: Introduce the concept of infinite series. Start with the harmonic series (sum of 1/n) and show it diverges. Contrast this with the p-series (sum of 1/n^s) where s > 1, which converges to a finite value. This sets the stage for defining the Zeta function as a sum.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Staircase of Blocks': If each block is 1/n wide, the staircase grows forever. But if we square the denominator (1/n²), the total width suddenly stops at exactly π²/6 (The Basel Problem).

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
sections.content: Formal definition of ζ(s) = Σ (1/n^s) for n=1 to infinity. Explain that 's' is the input variable. Transition from real numbers to complex numbers, explaining that 's' can be a complex coordinate (σ + it).
sections.example: An animation showing a 3D landscape where the X and Y axes are the real and imaginary parts of 's', and the vertical Z-axis is the magnitude of the Zeta function.

sections.title: The Euler Product: The Bridge to Primes
sections.content: The 'Magic' moment: Show how the sum over all integers is equal to the product over all prime numbers: ζ(s) = Π (1 - p^-s)^-1. This establishes the Zeta function as the ultimate tool for studying prime distribution.
sections.example: A 'Prime Sieve' machine: Imagine feeding all whole numbers into a machine on the left (the sum), and seeing prime-flavored 'gears' turning on the right (the product) to produce the exact same result.

sections.title: Analytic Continuation: Mapping the Unknown
sections.content: Explain that the original sum only works when the real part of s > 1. Introduce 'Analytic Continuation' as a way to 'extend' the function to the rest of the complex plane, revealing the 'Trivial' and 'Non-trivial' zeros.
sections.example: A 'Map Expansion' metaphor: Like a video game where the initial map is small, but a hidden formula allows the player to unlock the 'fog of war' and reveal the entire world.

sections.title: The Million Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis
sections.content: Define the Critical Strip (between 0 and 1) and the Critical Line (s = 1/2). Explain Riemann's prediction: all non-trivial zeros lie exactly on this line. Mention the $1 million Clay Mathematics Institute prize.
sections.example: A detective character, 'Professor Prime', pointing to a narrow tightrope (the 1/2 line). He notes that every 'treasure' (zero) found so far sits perfectly on this rope, but no one can prove they all do.

sections.title: Application: Cryptography and Prime Security
sections.content: Briefly connect the Zeta function to the Prime Number Theorem. Explain that understanding the 'music' of the Zeta zeros allows us to predict how primes are scattered. Mention the importance of primes in modern RSA encryption.
sections.example: A digital vault secured by a giant prime-number padlock. The Zeta function is described as the 'blueprints' to the vault; if we solve the Riemann Hypothesis, we understand the lock better than ever before.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Harmonic Series and Convergence
lecture_lines: Consider the infinite sum of one over n.
This harmonic series grows forever, never reaching a limit.
But squaring the denominator makes the total sum converge.
animations: Display the harmonic series formula $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n}$ in white (#FFFFFF) centered at the top.
Create a horizontal bar of blocks with widths 1, 0.5, 0.33, 0.25 colored cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate the bar growing indefinitely to the right, with 'Diverges' appearing in red (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
lecture_lines: Let's define the Riemann Zeta function for variable s.
It is the sum of n to the power negative s.
Initially, we consider s as a simple real number.
However, s can also be a complex coordinate.
This transforms the sum into a complex landscape.
animations: Show the Zeta function formula $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}$ in yellow (#FFFF00) at center.
Move the formula to the top and define $s = \sigma + it$ in blue (#50C8FF) below it.
Fade in a 2D grid representing the complex plane in gray (#808080).
Plot a pulsing dot at coordinate $s$ in magenta (#FF00FF).
Apply a colored gradient across the grid to visualize function magnitude.

storyboard.title: The Euler Product: The Bridge to Primes
lecture_lines: Leonhard Euler discovered a profound connection to prime numbers.
The infinite sum equals an infinite product of primes.
Each prime p contributes a unique factor to Zeta.
This formula bridges integers and the building blocks of math.
Zeta encodes the secret distribution of all prime numbers.
animations: Display the summation side $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^{-s}$ in white (#FFFFFF) on the left.
Display the product side $\prod_{p} (1-p^{-s})^{-1}$ in green (#00FF00) on the right.
Draw a glowing double-arrow bridge [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] in yellow (#FFFF00) between the two sides.
Highlight prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7 in the product symbol with a pulse effect.
Transform both sides into a single equation centered on screen.

storyboard.title: Analytic Continuation: Mapping the Unknown
lecture_lines: The original sum only works when s is large.
Analytic continuation extends the function across the entire plane.
This reveals hidden points where the function equals zero.
animations: Draw a vertical line at x=1 (#FFFFFF) with the right side shaded green (#00FF00).
Expand the green shading to cover the left side of the line in a smooth wave [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wave.svg].
Display the continuation formula in light blue (#ADD8E6) at the bottom.

storyboard.title: The Million Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis
lecture_lines: Most zeros sit on a single vertical line.
This critical line is where the real part is half.
Riemann hypothesized that every non-trivial zero lies here.
Proving this remains the greatest unsolved mystery in mathematics.
A million-dollar prize awaits whoever solves this puzzle.
animations: Mark the vertical boundaries x=0 and x=1 with gray lines (#808080).
Shade the 'Critical Strip' between them in light purple (#E6E6FA).
Draw a bold gold vertical line (#FFD700) at x=1/2.
Animate several small white dots (#FFFFFF) appearing exactly on the gold line.
Display '$1,000,000 Prize' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/money.svg] in large bold text at the top.

storyboard.title: Application: Cryptography and Prime Security
lecture_lines: Zeta's zeros act like the music of prime distribution.
Understanding this music helps us predict prime locations.
This security underpins modern digital encryption and privacy.
animations: Pulse a sequence of prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 along the bottom.
Place a silver padlock icon (#C0C0C0) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pad.svg] in the center of the screen.
Draw 'connections' (lines) from the Zeta zeros to the padlock.
